newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia sorghum harvest gains pace - Grainco.
newsitem.headline: Australia sorghum harvest gains pace - Grainco.

text.p: Australia's new crop sorghum harvest in south Queensland had gained some momentum as ground conditions improved and grain moisture levels declined, state grain co-operative Grainco Ltd said in its weekly market report.
Early quality reports indicated small grain may cause problems in those crops most severely affected by moisture stress, trading manager Rob Brealey said.
Further harvesting would occur this week if conditions were good, he said.
Brisbane sorghum values remained largely unchanged for the past week with buying interest subdued.
Planting got underway in central Queensland on an area expected to be at the lower end of forecasts, he said.
As ground conditions improved harvesters again tackled crops which had been affected by moisture.
Even with lower yield expectations of crops yet to be harvested and a smaller, later plant, production was still forecast to be greater than domestic demand.
Sorghum values were therefore taking direction from export values, with previous premiums diminishing for early harvested grain.
Consumers appear to have the majority of their expected requirements covered from February through to May, he said.
As the sorghhum harvest moved into full swing, further parcels of barley may appear as growers clear storages.
With this, most consumers would focus on the attractiveness of sorghum, limiting barley's upside, he said.
Domestic malting barley values declined over the past week, with Grainco's end-week bid at A$180.00 a tonne Brisbane.
Cottonseed activity remained light but constant over the week amid a wide range of market ideas on crop size and condition. Domestic oilseed values were steady to lower over the past week, he said.
